whole_case_success: All scientific items marked required_for_whole_case_success must pass, and evidence qualification must pass; no arbitrary threshold such as 60 points is used. The original rules assess recovery of a limited set of literature conclusions and do not establish a uniquely true mechanism.
numeric_comparison_policy: Retain the existing numerical targets/tolerances; first review comparability of physical identity, references and conditions. When comparability cannot be determined, mark needs_review and explain why; do not alter tolerances without authorization. Source numbers without assigned targets provide context only and are not implicit thresholds.
semantic_review_policy: A chemistry reviewer blinded to system identity assigns pass/fail/needs_review based on native computational evidence. Equivalent mechanisms supporting the same physical proposition are allowed; keyword matching alone is insufficient.

rules.expected: With the correct S_H molecular framework, electronic state and ring-closed/ring-opened references, actual calculations support ring opening being energetically uphill relative to the ring-closed state. The authors' radical cation serves as the reference model; equivalent models supported by actual evidence for the same ring-fate proposition are accepted. A ring-closed structure alone or observation of a ring-retained product is insufficient. This item does not require all H B1/B2 conformers or exact agreement with 5.8 or 3.2 kcal/mol.
rules.qualification: Must be supported by actual computational evidence from this run, with compatible species/configurations, composition, charge/spin, conditions, physical quantities and references. Labels, supplied observations or normal termination cannot substitute for this evidence.

rules.expected: Preserve the correct relative stereochemistry of S_Mcis, and support energetically favorable ring opening through actual ring-closed/ring-opened comparisons. The authors' main M06-2X model serves as the reference; species, references and energy conventions must correspond. Near-zero values obtained with other functionals or thermal corrections must not be presented as the same target. Both the main-text −2.5 and SI −0.8 kcal/mol values for cis-Me B2 are retained; neither is a uniquely specified exact target. The fine ordering of B1/B2 is outside this item.
rules.qualification: Must be supported by actual computational evidence from this run, with compatible species/configurations, composition, charge/spin, conditions, physical quantities and references. Labels, supplied observations or normal termination cannot substitute for this evidence.

rules.expected: Preserve the correct relative stereochemistry of S_Mtrans, and support ring opening being energetically uphill relative to the ring-closed state through actual ring-closed/ring-opened comparisons. The authors' main M06-2X model serves as the reference; other functionals in the source can change the sign, so assessment must use compatible physical definitions. Do not construct an uphill result by mixing methods. This item does not infer an independent experimental product distribution starting from trans, and sets no exact window around 1.8 or 2.1 kcal/mol.
rules.qualification: Must be supported by actual computational evidence from this run, with compatible species/configurations, composition, charge/spin, conditions, physical quantities and references. Labels, supplied observations or normal termination cannot substitute for this evidence.

rules.expected: With the same composition, the same charge/spin and a common energy zero, actual calculations support the trans ring-closed state of the methyl system being more stable than the cis ring-closed state and the relevant ring-opened states compared. cis/trans must be identified by molecular relative stereochemistry, not filenames alone. A difference between local ring-opening energies cannot replace a comparison across isomers using a common reference; the authors' B1/B2 labels or enumeration of all conformers are not additional quotas.
rules.qualification: Must be supported by actual computational evidence from this run, with compatible species/configurations, composition, charge/spin, conditions, physical quantities and references. Labels, supplied observations or normal termination cannot substitute for this evidence.

rules.expected: Preserve the S_Ptrans framework and relative stereochemistry. Actual structural/energy evidence must support a preference for ring opening in the tested branch, with no supported stable trap established in the ring-closing direction. The authors' profile showing increasing energy as the cleaved C–C bond is shortened, and optimization from a ring-closed structure to a ring-opened structure, serve as references; equivalent physical tests are allowed. A single ring-opened minimum is insufficient to establish this item. A finite profile does not establish the absence of ring-closed minima over the entire potential-energy surface, nor does it amount to a computed complete bimolecular dissociative electron-transfer trajectory.
rules.qualification: Must be supported by actual computational evidence from this run, with compatible species/configurations, composition, charge/spin, conditions, physical quantities and references. Labels, supplied observations or normal termination cannot substitute for this evidence.

rules.expected: The final answer integrates actual ring-reaction evidence for H, the methyl stereoisomers and Ph to show that ring-opening accessibility and ring-closed stability depend on substituents/stereochemistry; these N-cyclopropyl probes cannot universally be assumed to undergo fast irreversible ring opening upon oxidation. Within the compared models, cis-Me ring opening is more accessible than that of H and trans-Me, while the tested Ph branch favors ring opening more strongly. Actual comparisons supporting relative accessibility are required; reaction energies alone cannot serve as barriers. This conclusion does not require exact rates, fine B1/B2 ordering, or promotion of method-dependent source trends to a universal law.
rules.qualification: Must be supported by actual computational evidence from this run, with compatible species/configurations, composition, charge/spin, conditions, physical quantities and references. Labels, supplied observations or normal termination cannot substitute for this evidence.

rules.expected: The final answer connects actual evidence for methyl ring opening, the greater stability of the trans ring-closed state under a common reference, and the public observation that trans appears after starting from cis. Together, these support a compatible explanation in which ring opening can lead to the more stable trans ring-closed state; evidence-supported alternative routes establishing the same conversion relationship are allowed. The additional conclusion explains the observed isomerization; merely listing an energy ordering is insufficient. Do not describe this explanation as having established a separate isomerization barrier, rate or equilibrium ratio, and do not introduce a new target for the product distribution starting from trans.
rules.qualification: Must be supported by actual computational evidence from this run, with compatible species/configurations, composition, charge/spin, conditions, physical quantities and references. Labels, supplied observations or normal termination cannot substitute for this evidence.

scientific_rubric.description: Ring opening of the H-substituted system is unfavorable within the compared model
cis-Me ring opening is favorable within a compatible reference model
trans-Me ring opening is unfavorable within a compatible reference model
The trans ring-closed state of the methyl system is lower in energy than the cis ring-closed state and the relevant ring-opened states
The Ph-substituted system favors ring opening in the tested branch
Final conclusion: substituent and stereochemical effects rule out a universal assumption of fast irreversible ring opening
Final conclusion: ring opening and the more stable trans ring-closed state explain cis→trans conversion

scope_changes: The scope is narrowed to ring fate after oxidation; oxidation-potential, aldehyde/isotope and full light-dependence items are removed. The 7 retained items are reweighted to a total of 100 points. No new ARCHE results were used to fit the scores.
reference_issues: The cis-Me B2 reaction energy of −2.5 in the main text conflicts with approximately −0.8 in the SI; this task assigns no numerical acceptance window to this scalar. Near-zero energy differences and ordering changes across methods are reviewed using compatible models.
source_location: Main text p7 Table 3/Fig.9; SI p49–51
